articles.title: Watch orcas ram a sunfish so hard it explodes
articles.text:
There have been numerous accounts in recent years of orcas ramming boats—and sometimes sinking them. Scientists believe this may be a form of culturally learned behavior passed down through generations. Now we have fresh examples: orcas in the Gulf of California were filmed teaming up to ram sunfish with so much force that the carcasses exploded into small fragments. While orcas have been known to use force to remove flesh from prey, this is something different, according to a new paper published in the journal Frontiers in Ethology.
“We think this may help younger orcas feed more easily, or it could also just be for fun,” said co-author Kathryn Ayres of Beneath The Waves, a nonprofit organization promoting ocean health. “Orcas are known for playing with their food.”
Orcas engage in cooperative hunting strategies that can involve striking or killing animals—sometimes eating their prey, sometimes not—so the behavior could be described as social interaction, play, or practice as a mode of social learning. Orcas have been observed ramming whale sharks as another orca held the prey steady. Other cooperative strategies include herding mobile rays, blocking an escape path while hunting white sharks, and deliberately producing waves to bump penguins off ice floes.
When hunting species like sunfish, orcas typically rely on a three-pronged strategy. First, an orca will target the pectoral fins, then slash the sunfish across its body to remove the viscera. After that, the orca will use its beak to get at the remaining tissue. The newly observed “ram-to-fragment” behavior might represent a more sophisticated version of that basic strategy.
Play with your food
The first instance occurred in July 2024 off the coast of San Jose del Cabo in Mexico. A tourism operator filmed three adult female orcas, one male, and one juvenile catching and eating a spine-tail devil ray. Just after, the same operator filmed one of the adult females holding the carcass of a sunfish in her mouth. The sunfish had a large lateral wound, so the viscera had likely already been removed. The male orca then charged at the carcass, with the female releasing it just before impact. There was an audible sound upon impact as the carcass fragmented and bits of flesh dispersed in the water. The juvenile orca proceeded to eat the smaller fragments while the adults fed on what remained of the split-open body.

articles.title: Cato Networks and CrowdStrike partner to unify network and endpoint security - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cato Networks and CrowdStrike partner to unify network and endpoint security
Networking and security company Cato Networks Ltd. today unveiled a partnership with CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. to integrate their platforms and give security teams a single view of network and endpoint data.
The integration ties the Cato SASE Platform to the CrowdStrike Falcon platform. Analysts get endpoint alerts and network activity side by side, which the companies say should shorten investigations and speed response.
Network and endpoint monitoring usually sit in separate tools. An analyst chasing an alert in one has to go dig up the matching activity in the other, which is slow and leaves room to miss things. Cato and CrowdStrike say wiring the two feeds together removes that manual step and gives detections more context to draw on.
The integrations cover three areas. Cato XOps and CrowdStrike Falcon Discover correlate endpoint detections with network telemetry to sharpen threat visibility and accelerate investigations. Cato Asset Security and Falcon Discover combine device intelligence with endpoint context for a fuller view of managed assets. The Cato SASE Platform also streams network telemetry into Falcon Next-Gen SIEM, letting analysts hunt threats and build detections from a broader set of signals.
“Security outcomes, especially in the AI era, can only improve when fueled by rich and connected data,” said Karl Soderlund, global channel chief at Cato Networks. “This partnership further enhances Cato’s ability to deliver complete visibility, full context and agentic control to make security operations teams more effective in defending against the next wave of AI threats.”
Chris Stewart, vice president of global cloud and technology alliance partners at CrowdStrike, said integrating the two platforms lets customers correlate network and endpoint telemetry, streamline investigations and respond to threats faster.
The integrations also reach customers through distribution. Francisco Criado, senior vice president of security, cloud and AI at TD SYNNEX Corp., said the collaboration gives channel partners a more integrated approach to security that simplifies deployment and scales more easily.
The technical integrations are generally available to customers worldwide through the CrowdStrike Marketplace.
Cato Networks is a venture capital-backed company that was valued at more than $4.8 billion in its most recent funding round of $359 million in June 2025.

articles.title: DC has released a fresh trailer for its body horror movie 'Clayface' — and the Batman villain's first-ever solo film is going to make my skin crawl in the best way possible
articles.text:
The new trailer for Clayface is pure nightmare fuel — here's everything you need to know about the forthcoming body horror comic book movie
- DC Studios has released the official trailer for body-horror movie Clayface
- It'll take shape in theaters worldwide on October 23
- Viewers have plenty of questions about the forthcoming DC Universe film
DC Studios has released a new trailer for its next movie Clayface — and, as someone who's not a fan of body horror, it made me squeamish in the best way possible.
The forthcoming DC Universe (DCU) film, which will take shape in theaters worldwide on October 23, will see the Batman villain star in his first-ever solo flick. And, while its latest round of footage answers some big questions that audiences had about the comic book movie, it leaves casual viewers with even more.
Indeed, the teaser might finally pull back the curtain on how the titular shapeshifting character is created and why he embarks on a Gotham City-based quest for revenge. Nevertheless, there are myriad questions that the DCU Chapter One film's latest trailer, which arrived three months after Clayface's first "super freaky" trailer, leaves unanswered.
For what it's worth, my guide on everything we know so far about Clayface provides clarity on some of the queries that are likely rattling around your head. If you don't have time to read through that extensive article right now, though, I've moulded a quick-fire Q&A below that'll shed light on your biggest burning questions. Bear in mind that potential spoilers immediately follow for Clayface, so proceed at your own risk.
Is Clayface in the same universe as The Batman?
Let's get one of the most notable questions out of the way first: no, Clayface is not set in The Batman Universe.
That franchise, which stars Robert Pattinson as the titular vigilante and is helmed by Matt Reeves, is a completely separate entity to James Gunn's DCU. It's the latter — which also comprises Superman, Supergirl, Creature Commandos, and Lanterns — that Clayface is a part of.
Will Batman be in Clayface?
Another popular query I've seen floating around the internet since Clayface's second trailer dropped. In short: no, Batman isn't expected to appear in this film.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"Why not?" you might ask. The short answer is Gunn and Safran haven't started the search for the DCU's Batman, let alone publicly announced which actor will play him.
Unless a stand-in — one likely silhouetted against the background, like the legendary Caped Crusader was in episode 6 of Creature Commandos on HBO Max — makes the briefest of cameos in Clayface, then, I'd temper your expectations over a possible appearance from the Dark Knight.
Is this the same Clayface who appeared in Creature Commandos?
Yes. Speaking to Entertainment Weekly, Safran confirmed that the Clayface who appears in this film is the same one who had a role to play in Creature Commandos season 1.
Prior to Safran's comments on the matter, there had been some confusion as to which Clayface we'd see in this movie. After all, there have been numerous iterations of the character in DC Comics. Of that contingent, Basil Karlo and Matt Hagen are the most famous — and it's the second of that pair who'll not only appear in Clayface, but who also showed up in Creature Commandos.
Where does Clayface sit on the DCU timeline?
Clayface is the fifth DCU Chapter One project that'll see the light of day. Timeline-wise, though, it'll be the first one that audiences should watch if they choose to watch the DCU films and TV shows in chronological order — Gunn confirming as much on Threads in April.
Who plays Clayface?
That'll be Tom Rhys Harries, a Welsh actor who some readers will recognize from Doctor Who episode 'Dot and Bubble'.
According to Gunn, he and fellow DC Studios co-head Peter Safran were "blown away" by Harries' audition for Clayface's lead role. Based on the footage we've seen this far, Harries seems like a great fit for the character, but we'll have to wait until the movie is actually released to be able to put Gunn's comments into their full context.
How did Clayface become Clayface? What's the plot of the DCU movie?
Where the latter question is concerned, here's the flick's updated story synopsis: "Matt Hagen’s meteoric rise from Gotham street kid to Hollywood leading man is tragically cut short when a local crime boss' actions leave him horribly disfigured.
"Abandoned by his team and with nothing left, Matt seeks out a cutting edge treatment that miraculously returns him to his former self… but, also unexpectedly affects his grip on reality, spiraling him down a destructive path of all-consuming revenge."
As for Harries' Matt Hagen becomes the tragic, metamorphosizing villain, Clayface's latest trailer and plot brief confirm that he'll be patient zero for an experimental serum that initially seems to heal him. However, it doesn't take long for this ground-breaking treatment's side effects to *ahem* take shape and turn him into a transmutating monster.
What are Clayface's powers?
As his villainous alias implies, Clayface's mud-like physiology gives him the ability to mould his body in any way he sees fit. That means he can grow and shrink in size, alter his density at will, and is impervious to traditional physical attacks, including punches, kicks, and all kinds of weapons.
Furthermore, the metahuman possesses superhuman strength, durability, and reflexes. Lastly, he has the ability to regenerate, although that's a process that takes a long time, especially if, say, he's torn apart by an explosion of some sort.
Who's written and directed Clayface?
Horror auteur Mike Flanagan is the main man behind Clayface's story. However, Hossein Amini (Obi-Wan Kenobi, 47 Ronin) also helped to pen its screenplay.
As for its filmmaker, James Watkins is the man behind the camera. His directing credits include Speak No Evil, The Woman in Black, and Black Mirror episode 'Shut Up and Dance'.
What is Clayface's movie rating?
Perhaps unsurprisingly, Clayface will carry a hard R-rating in the US. That's the equivalent of an 18 age rating in the UK and an Restricted (R18+) rating in Australia.
The DCU's other films in Superman and Supergirl were suitable for kids accompanied by an adult, but this one certainly won't be. Expect plenty more gross body horror moments, hyperviolent action, and other mature content to be woven through its sub-two hour runtime.
For more DCU coverage, find out everything we know so far about Lanterns and get the full lowdown on Superman film sequel Man of Tomorrow.

articles.title: Github stellt Bug-Bounty-Programm um: Wie dadurch die KI-Flut eingedämmt werden soll
articles.text:
Im Kampf gegen KI-Flut: Github strukturiert Bug-Bounty-Programm um
KI-Tools können dabei helfen, Schwachstellen in Software schneller aufzudecken. Die Programme haben aber auch dafür gesorgt, dass zahlreiche KI-generierte Meldungen eintrudeln, die keinerlei tatsächliche Fehler beinhalten. Schon Linux-Entwickler Linus Torvalds machte seinem Ärger über KI-generierte Fehlermeldungen Luft. Und ein Open-Source-Projekt musste sein Bug-Bounty-Programm komplett abstellen, weil es von den Meldungen überwältigt wurde. Jetzt zieht auch Github Konsequenzen aus der steigenden Zahl der KI-Berichte.
Github: So funktioniert das neue Bug-Bounty-Programm
In der Ankündigung zeigt Github, dass es künftig zwei verschiedene Stufen im Bug-Bounty-Programm gibt. Die Verantwortlichen führen zunächst ein VIP-Programm ein. Hierfür qualifizieren sich alle Bug-Jäger:innen, die „konsistent hochqualitative“ Berichte abgeben, die eine gravierende Auswirkung haben. Für VIPs gibt es mehrere Vorteile. Für einen Bug bekommen sie mehr Geld, können schneller mit GitHub-Entwickler:innen kommunizieren und arbeiten sogar eng mit ihnen für Lösungen zusammen.
Schwachstellen mit einem geringen Gefahrenfaktor bringen VIPs schon 1.000 US-Dollar. Mit steigendem Risiko für die Plattform, steigt auch die Belohnung an. Für kritische Sicherheitslücken verspricht GitHub Beträge ab 30.000 Dollar. Um sich als VIP zu qualifizieren, müssen Bug-Jäger:innen eine bestimmte Anzahl an Fehlern gefunden haben. Dabei reicht schon eine kritische Sicherheitslücke, zwei mit einem hohen Gefahren-Score, für mit einem mittleren Risiko oder sieben Bugs mit niedrigem Score.
Daneben steht das öffentliche Programm für alle Bug-Jäger:innen. Hier passt Github die Belohnungen nach unten an, um Qualität über Quantität zu priorisieren. Geringfügige Schwachstellen bringen den Bug-Huntern jetzt noch 250 Dollar ein. Zuvor waren es zwischen 617 und 2.000 Dollar. Für kritische Lücken gibt es jetzt noch maximal 10.000 Dollar. Hier hatte Github zuvor 20.000 bis 30.000 Dollar angesetzt.
Ebenfalls relevant für alle künftigen Bug-Jäger:innen: Wer bislang noch keine Berichte eingereicht hat, kann künftig maximal vier Bugs melden. Die Begrenzung realisiert Github – wie schon die Zulassung für das VIP-Programm – über die Plattform Hackerone. GithHub schreibt dazu: „Das ist keine Wand für neue Forscher. Die Plattform von Hackerone gibt Forschern, die die Anforderungen nicht erfüllen, vier anfängliche Einreichungen, was genug für Neulinge ist, um echte Funde und ihre Fertigkeiten zu präsentieren.“ Erst wer sich beweist, darf künftig mehr Fehler melden.

articles.title: Etched Raises $300M with $1B in Pre-Orders - EE Times
articles.text:
SAN JOSE, Calif. — AI chip startup Etched has raised $300 million in a Series C round at a $10 billion pre-money valuation, bringing the total raised to $1.1 billion. Etched’s round was led by Sequoia with participation from A16Z, Jane Street, Blackstone, SK Hynix, Diffusion Capital, plus existing investors.
The company already has $1 billion in pre-orders, Etched president Robert Wachen told EE Times on a recent visit to the company’s San Jose headquarters.
“In general, we are focused on the biggest AI companies and the biggest AI clusters in the world,” Wachen said. “Our customers are buying many billions of dollars of hardware… we expect that the product will be very good for coding, long context, long horizon agents, and a lot of things that inference tokens are going to be used for.”
Customers are already running their workloads remotely in Etched’s data center with results that are “significantly better than anything on the market”, Wachen said.
In addition to the cluster and lab up and running in the company’s San Jose office, Etched recently opened a new R&D facility in Milpitas, Calif., which includes a 10 MW data center plus a lab and quick turn SMT line.
Workload flexibility
Etched, started by Harvard dropouts Gavin Uberti and Chris Zhu with Harvard graduate Robert Wachen, attracted attention two years ago when it said it could beat Nvidia Blackwell-based systems’ token throughput by an order of magnitude using chips that “burned the transformer architecture into hardware”. Today, the technical story has evolved a bit, Wachen said, but the company’s aims are just as ambitious.
“Early on, we tried a bunch of different ideas, some very radical, like hard-coding a specific model or a specific model architecture into hardware,” he said. “What we realized is that the world needs a new computing paradigm that enables more FLOPS and bandwidth, that can run any type of inference workload, whether that’s multi-trillion parameter MoE models, or diffusion, or state-space models.”
More flexibility on workloads is part of Etched’s technical evolution, along with a broader focus on system and cluster-level topologies, in keeping with industry trends, Wachen said.
EE Times visited the Etched office in San Jose for a tour of the lab and an impressive large MoE inference demo, and was able to see racks of hardware up and running in prefill and decode configurations. Etched declined to make performance figures public at this stage, however.
Vertical integration
The company is vertically integrated, since its ambitious design has meant taking on parts of the stack other fabless startups usually wouldn’t. Every part of Etched’s rack, from the ASIC design to custom packaging, board design and cooling to server and infrastructure design, was done in-house, Wachen said.
“We’re deep believers in vertical integration,” he said. “It’s not enough to build a chip, it’s not enough to build the server, it’s not enough to build the rack, it’s not even enough to build a cluster. You have to build a machine that can produce the best clusters in the world at gigawatt scale.”
Etched is both dogmatic and pragmatic about its vertically integrated approach, Wachen said. The overall aim is simply to do what it takes to serve more tokens than the competition. It’s a big ask for a startup, but the team is over 450 and growing.
Low-voltage inference
A big part of Etched’s performance comes from utilization, which indirectly comes from turning down the voltage for parts of its chips. Today’s big AI chips suffer from thermal issues, which means cores have to be throttled (clock frequency reduced to reduce heat loss), with a resulting loss in performance.
Etched is running the transistors in its math engines at “under half” the voltage other AI chips use in a scheme it calls low-voltage inference (LVI). This enables more FLOPS per Watt, and it also means better utilization of those FLOPS, Wachen said, since throttling isn’t required. The company can run at 80%+ utilization for trillion-parameter MoE models without thermal throttling.
“The current state of affairs is that for every FLOPS I buy, I’m really getting 0.2 to 0.4 FLOPS,” he said. “If every chip in the world ran LVI, we could double or triple the world’s inference capacity.”
There is a reason sub-threshold designs are generally limited to small chips (such as Ambiq’s microcontrollers) and crypto-mining ASICs. Running at low voltage means extremely high current, with resulting challenges in handling current spikes, and in general the clock frequencies that can be achieved are very slow.
“This is an extremely hard physical problem,” Wachen said. “There’s tons of innovations across the stack from things at the fabrication level, things at the ASIC design, packaging, board, cooling and mechanical levels. Everything has to go together to make this happen.”
Will Etched have to reduce its clock frequency significantly to make it all work?
“Not necessarily,” Wachen said. “Of course, it’s hard to run a high clock speed at low voltage, mainly because the current goes up, but there are ways to solve these problems. One of the breakthroughs is how to run at much lower voltages than GPUs or other AI chips while being able to run a much larger amount of silicon.”
Part of the solution is running only the math engines at lower voltage; the chip’s SRAM blocks can’t (sub-threshold operation isn’t possible today for standard SRAM cells as it reduces the stability too much). For this reason, competitors’ designs that finely mix compute and SRAM would find low-voltage operation harder, Wachen said.
“These are hard problems to be solved, but our hardware is the proof we’ve found a solution,” he said.
Etched’s chip is on TSMC N4P, and it’s a full-reticle-sized design with six stacks of HBM. Wachen said the chip deliberately uses a different process node, different packaging technology, and different memory than Nvidia’s next-generation Rubin GPUs to enable both to get to scale simultaneously.
Cluster-scale memory
Another of Etched’s key innovations is a low-latency shared memory pool across a whole cluster in a single scale-up domain using a custom high-bandwidth interconnect for fast access to both SRAM and HBM across chips.
“That meant both a new type of interconnect and a new type of memory subsystem had to be co-designed throughout the stack to make it possible,” Wachen said. “And we need to do that with technologies that exist and are mass-producible today, including copper.”
In Etched’s lab, the company has split prefill and decode stages across separate racks of Etched chips, and can easily handle both because of their compute and bandwidth, Wachen said. That said, Etched would be just as happy to be deployed alongside other hardware in a disaggregated setup, he added.
Etched racks will start shipping to customers this summer.

articles.title: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, July 23, 2026.
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 23, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, July 23, 2026.
Community agriculture is the way forward for farmers to enhance their livelihoods even as Indian startups continue to raise funding, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors
This woman entrepreneur is helping small farmers earn more through community-supported agriculture
Spudnik Farms, founded by Sumeet Kaur, connects urban consumers with local farmers through a subscription model. The company works with 250 farmers across Karnataka, helping them earn higher incomes while promoting seasonal, indigenous and sustainably grown produce.
Funding news
Banking tech company BusinessNext raises $40M from ServiceNow
Workplace management software company ServiceNow has announced an investment of $40 million in BusinessNext, a Noida-headquartered technology firm focused on banking and financial services industry. The Series C round has valued BusinessNext at $700 million and is aimed at strengthening the company's efforts to drive autonomous operations and private AI solutions across banking and financial services.
Tech30 startup CARPL.ai raises $10M in Series A led by IFC
CARPL.ai, a radiology AI marketplace and enterprise platform, has raised $10 million in a Series A round of funding led by International Finance Corporation (IFC), the private sector arm of the World Bank Group, with participation from Stellaris Venture Partners and other investors. CARPL.ai was part of the YourStory Tech30 cohort of 2022.
Farm Watt Innovations raises Rs 32.5 Cr to expand bioenergy network
Farm Watt Innovations has raised Rs 32.5 crore in a funding round co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter to strengthen India's bioenergy supply chain. The climate-focused agribusiness converts agricultural waste into biomass for compressed biogas (CBG) plants and other renewable energy applications, helping reduce stubble burning and greenhouse gas emissions while creating rural livelihoods.
The fresh capital will be used to expand biomass collection networks, establish additional aggregation hubs, invest in machinery and strengthen its workforce. Going forward, the company plans to develop its own portfolio of CBG, bio-pellet and biochar plants, creating an integrated circular bioeconomy platform that delivers environmental, social and economic benefits.
Wiffy secures $3 million Series A funding
Home improvement services platform Wiffy has raised $3 million in a Series A funding round led by Earth Fund, with participation from Persol Holdings of Japan and existing investor Capria Ventures. The company provides post-sales installation and maintenance services for more than 100 brands, including IKEA, Panasonic, Godrej, Hettich and Amazon.
The proceeds will be used to enhance its technology platform, strengthen AI-powered workforce management, expand enterprise partnerships and enter new service categories. Wiffy operates through a network of over 5,000 certified technicians and has served more than one million homes across 100 cities, while maintaining a business model driven primarily by enterprise partnerships.
NeuralKart raises Rs 2.35 Cr in seed funding
AI-powered insurtech startup NeuralKart has raised Rs 2.35 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures. The Bengaluru-based company develops AI-driven decision-making tools that automate insurance underwriting, claims processing and industrial safety assessments. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen product development, expand AI and machine learning capabilities, and accelerate customer acquisition and go-to-market initiatives.
NeuralKart said it has already secured paying enterprise customers and maintains a 100% customer retention rate. The company works with leading insurers and industrial risk services firms and has also entered into a co-development partnership for its FieldSense platform, targeting the growing insurance automation and industrial safety technology markets.
Upkraft secures Rs 1.6 Cr in pre-seed round
AI-powered extracurricular learning platform Upkraft has raised Rs 1.6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by PedalStart, with participation from angel investors, entrepreneurs and early-stage ecosystem players. Founded by Tejasvi Singh Kushwah, Varun Mangal and Kritika Varandani, the startup offers structured extracurricular learning programmes for students at homes, schools and residential communities.
The company will use the proceeds to develop AI-powered personalised learning tools, expand operations across Bengaluru and Gurugram, strengthen its technology platform and build teams across product, engineering, sales and tutor operations. Over the next 12 to 18 months, Upkraft aims to increase student enrolments and deepen its presence in key markets.
Other news
Utho Cloud to deploy 10,000 GPUs for sovereign AI
Utho Cloud has announced plans to deploy 10,000 GPUs over the next seven to eight quarters to strengthen India's sovereign AI infrastructure. The investment will include NVIDIA's H200, H100, A100, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and L4 GPUs, enabling enterprises, startups, researchers and government organisations to access high-performance AI computing hosted entirely within India.
The company said its platform will offer predictable pricing in Indian rupees, guaranteed GPU availability, data residency compliant with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act and 24x7 support. With more than 51,000 users, Utho aims to reduce dependence on overseas cloud infrastructure while providing secure AI computing capabilities for domestic organisations.
Google concludes Build with AI parliamentary showcase
Google has concluded the Parliamentary Showcase of its Build with AI: Code for Communities programme, an initiative aimed at connecting AI innovation with public governance. Organised with The Dialogue, the programme saw 12 winning developer teams present AI-powered solutions before Members of Parliament.
More than 7,000 developers from over 18 Indian cities participated, creating over 1,000 open-source projects using Google's Gemini and Gemma AI models. The solutions addressed civic governance, public health, agriculture and environmental challenges. Google said selected projects will now be piloted in parliamentary constituencies, demonstrating how AI can be used to improve public service delivery and community welfare across the country.
Cars24 Labs partners Startup Policy Forum on AI
Cars24 Labs, the AI innovation arm of Cars24, has partnered with the Startup Policy Forum (SPF) to support responsible AI adoption and policy development in India. Under the partnership, Cars24 Labs will contribute to AI policy discussions, founder engagements, industry dialogues and global immersion programmes while sharing practical insights from deploying AI across its business. SPF represents more than 75 new-age companies and works to strengthen India's startup ecosystem. The collaboration aims to bring together founders, policymakers, researchers and technology leaders to exchange ideas and help shape AI policy. Cars24 Labs said the initiative reflects its commitment to supporting India's emergence as a global leader in artificial intelligence.
Cashfree Payments waives gateway fees for new merchants
Cashfree Payments has introduced a limited-period offer waiving payment gateway charges for new businesses on the first Rs 20 lakh of gross merchandise value (GMV) processed through its platform until March 31, 2027. The initiative is aimed at helping small and growing businesses improve cash flow ahead of the festive season. Besides the fee waiver, new merchants will benefit from onboarding within minutes, next-day settlements and dedicated account managers during the peak sales period. Cashfree said the move will allow businesses to reinvest savings into inventory, marketing and logistics while simplifying digital payments and reducing operational costs for small and medium enterprises.
Wipro Consumer Care acquires Good Home and Eva brands
Wipro Consumer Care & Lighting has signed definitive agreements to acquire the Good Home and Eva brands from TTK Healthcare Ltd. for Rs 256 crore. The acquisition strengthens Wipro's presence in the home care and personal care segments. Good Home offers products including air fresheners, scrubbers and drain cleaners, while Eva is among India's established deodorant brands with body sprays, perfumes, roll-ons and talcum powders. Together, the two brands generated Rs 148 crore in revenue during FY26. Wipro said the acquisition aligns with its strategy of expanding into trusted, high-growth consumer categories driven by rising hygiene awareness, premiumisation and evolving lifestyle preferences.
Campus Fund appoints Howard Morgan to advisory board
Campus Fund, a venture capital firm focused on student- and dropout-led startups, has appointed veteran investor Dr. Howard L. Morgan to its Global Advisory Board. Morgan is Chair and General Partner at B Capital and co-founder of First Round Capital, an early investor in companies including Uber, Square, Roblox and Notion. His appointment comes as Campus Fund deploys its third and largest fund— a $100 million corpus announced in June 2025 — to support up to 60 startups over four years. The fund evaluates more than 7,000 startups annually through a network of over 100 student scouts, with investments spanning deeptech, space technology and climate technology.
Quest Global named leader in ISG semiconductor study
Engineering services firm Quest Global has been recognised as a Leader in the ISG Provider Lens Semiconductor Industry Services and Solutions 2026 Study for the US market. The company earned leadership positions in Design, Test and Verification Services and Manufacturing and Engineering Services. ISG highlighted Quest Global's capabilities across silicon engineering, custom SoC and ASIC development, embedded systems and manufacturing engineering. The report also recognised the company's "Silicon to Systems to Cloud" approach and AI-enabled engineering methodologies, which help semiconductor companies reduce design cycles, improve first-pass silicon success and accelerate the development of next-generation semiconductor products.
InCred Asset Management crosses Rs 1,000 crore healthcare AUM
InCred Asset Management has crossed Rs 1,000 crore in investments across listed healthcare companies through its portfolio management services, becoming one of India's largest dedicated healthcare PMS providers. Launched in February 2021, the healthcare strategy has delivered a 18.97% CAGR, outperforming the BSE 500 TRI's 13.27% CAGR, according to the company. The portfolios invest across pharmaceuticals, hospitals, diagnostics, medical technology and contract research businesses. InCred said the milestone reflects growing investor confidence in India's healthcare sector, supported by structural factors such as rising healthcare spending, expanding insurance coverage, favourable demographics and increasing innovation in healthcare services.
Konnect Insights launches AI-powered Research Cloud
Customer experience platform Konnect Insights has launched Konnect Research Cloud (KRC), an AI-powered intelligence platform designed to help enterprises analyse customer data across multiple systems using natural language queries. The platform connects with existing customer-facing technology stacks and delivers evidence-backed insights in seconds to support business decision-making. KRC marks the first step towards the company's vision of building a Front Office Operating System that unifies enterprise technologies through AI. The solution is immediately available to enterprise customers worldwide. Konnect Insights operates cloud infrastructure across India, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the US, the UK and Germany to ensure compliance with regional data residency requirements.
PhysicsWallah partners NWWA to support Navy families
Education company PhysicsWallah (PW) has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Indian Navy Welfare & Wellness Association (NWWA) to provide educational support to the families of Indian Navy personnel. Under the initiative, families of Navy martyrs and personnel who died during service will receive full scholarships, while serving and retired personnel's families will be eligible for discounts on PW's offline coaching and online courses. The scholarships cover preparation for competitive examinations including JEE, NEET, UPSC, SSC CGL and state public service commissions. Applications will be jointly verified by NWWA and PW, with the programme aimed at making quality education more accessible to defence families across India.
FincFriends reports 43% growth in assets under management
Digital lending NBFC FincFriends reported a 43% year-on-year increase in assets under management to Rs 875 crore in FY26, while revenue rose 33% to Rs 999 crore. Loan disbursements during the year climbed to Rs 3,732 crore, compared with Rs 2,585 crore in the previous fiscal. The company said it has served more than 5.5 million borrowers since inception and currently processes around 3,000 digital loans every day. Looking ahead, FincFriends plans to expand its customer base, strengthen partnerships, improve portfolio quality and grow its near-prime lending business through higher-ticket loans, supported by a profitable business model and strong institutional backing.
Workday launches AI-powered learning platform with Sana
Workday has announced the general availability of Workday Learning, powered by Sana, an AI-driven learning solution designed to deliver personalised employee training. The platform combines Workday's workforce and skills data with Sana's AI capabilities to provide tailored learning recommendations, AI tutoring and automated course creation. Administrators can also use AI to streamline assignments and learning campaigns, reducing manual effort. The integrated solution is now available globally for Workday Human Capital Management customers, while Sana Learn will also be offered as a standalone product for organisations not using Workday's HR or financial management platforms.
StraitsMicro unveils sovereign surveillance chip family
Singapore-based StraitsMicro has unveiled Visora, a sovereign camera System-on-Chip (SoC) family designed as an indigenous alternative for surveillance systems following India's restrictions on Chinese surveillance chips. The new semiconductor platform is aimed at government, defence, smart city and critical infrastructure applications in India and overseas. Developed with Bengaluru-based design partner Proxelera and distributor Aqtronics, Visora features AI acceleration, low-power multicore processors, advanced video compression and edge AI capabilities including facial recognition, crowd analytics and behavioural analysis. The company said the platform supports India's drive towards secure, locally developed semiconductor technologies for surveillance infrastructure.
Bijliride expands student EV rental programme
Electric mobility platform Bijliride has expanded its Project Udaan initiative by launching a student-focused electric two-wheeler rental programme across major Indian cities. The scheme offers flexible, zero-commitment EV rentals while integrating optional micro-gig delivery opportunities that allow students to offset their daily rental costs. The company said the initiative addresses commuting challenges and promotes financial independence without requiring long working hours. Bijliride has reported steady growth in registrations across Hyderabad, Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi-NCR, with students using the vehicles for internships, examinations and skill development programmes. The company believes the initiative will encourage sustainable mobility and increase electric vehicle adoption among young consumers.
Enmovil appoints Jayaraman Krishnamurthy as global sales head
AI-native supply chain orchestration platform Enmovil Solutions has appointed Jayaraman Krishnamurthy as its Head of Global Sales to drive international expansion across India, the US and the Asia-Pacific region. Krishnamurthy brings over 25 years of experience in enterprise software, manufacturing and supply chain, having held leadership roles at Asian Paints, SAP, Capillary Technologies and o9 Solutions. In his new role, he will lead the company's global sales strategy and strengthen its presence in key international markets. Enmovil said the appointment comes as manufacturers increasingly adopt digital supply chain solutions, positioning the company to capitalise on growing global demand for AI-driven supply chain intelligence platforms.
ePlane, Apollo Hospitals partner on electric air ambulances
The ePlane Company and Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd. have signed a memorandum of understanding to introduce electric air ambulances and medical delivery drones into India's emergency healthcare network. Under the partnership, ePlane's e200X aircraft will be deployed for rapid inter-hospital patient transfers, trauma care, cardiac emergencies and organ transport, while its subsidiary Amber Wings will provide drones for transporting blood, medicines, vaccines and diagnostic samples.
Apollo will explore potential orders for the aircraft and drones and may consider a strategic investment in ePlane. The companies will also work with aviation regulators to develop the infrastructure needed for advanced air mobility in healthcare.
Vertiv names Raghavendra Kale India channel leader
Critical digital infrastructure provider Vertiv has promoted Raghavendra Kale as its Channel Leader for India. In his new role, Kale will lead the company's channel sales strategy, expand its partner ecosystem and strengthen engagement across key reseller and distribution segments. He previously served as Director, West Zone, Channel, where he played a key role in improving operations and driving business growth. With nearly three decades of industry experience, Kale is expected to help scale Vertiv's partner-led business strategy while nurturing strategic accounts and expanding the company's market reach in India amid growing demand for digital infrastructure solutions.
BULLET appoints Apurba Sen as VP, Business Strategy & Sales
Microdrama platform BULLET, backed by ZEE Entertainment Enterprises, has appointed Apurba Sen as Vice President, Business Strategy & Sales. The appointment comes after the launch of Trinetra AI, the company's AI-powered filmmaking and content intelligence platform.
Sen will oversee strategic initiatives across BULLET Microdrama, Trinetra AI and future business ventures, focusing on partnerships, fundraising, commercial expansion and international growth. He brings more than two decades of experience in advertising technology, streaming, connected TV, AI-driven creative technologies and digital platforms. The company said the appointment strengthens its leadership team as it expands its AI-enabled entertainment ecosystem.

articles.title: Le smartphone cause-t-il le cancer du cerveau ? Après 28 ans d’études, la science livre son verdict
articles.text:
Le smartphone cause-t-il le cancer du cerveau ? Après 28 ans d’études, la science livre son verdict
Qui ne s’est jamais demandé si garder son smartphone collé à l’oreille pouvait finir par être dangereux ? Après avoir passé au crible 63 études, 28 ans de données, des scientifiques apportent une réponse rassurante. Leur vaste analyse ne trouve aucun lien entre l’usage du smartphone et les cancers du cerveau, de la tête ou du cou.
Le smarthpone collé à l'oreille provoque-t-il le cancer ? La question taraude les esprits depuis l'essor de la téléphonie mobile dans les années 2000, nourrie par la classification des radiofréquences comme "peut-être cancérogènes" (groupe 2B) par le Centre international de recherche sur le cancer (CIRC) en 2013. En France, l'ANSES était parvenue à la même conclusion en novembre 2025, après avoir passé au crible près de mille études.
Sarah Diepstraten et John (Eddie) La Marca, chercheurs au Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research (WEHI, Australie), publient le 17 juillet 2026 dans The Conversation une synthèse des 13 revues commandées par l'OMS en 2019, dont celle qu'ils ont eux-mêmes cosignée. Leur verdict est limpide : les données disponibles ne montrent aucune association entre ondes radio et cancers du cerveau, de la tête ou du cou.
63 études passées au crible sur près de trois décennies
La revue princeps, publiée dans Environment International, pilotée par Ken Karipidis de l'autorité australienne de radioprotection (ARPANSA), a ratissé plus de 5 000 publications parues entre 1994 et 2022 pour en retenir 63, jugées méthodologiquement exploitables.
Cette revue systématique repose sur un ensemble de données bien plus large que celui examiné par le CIRC, incluant des études plus récentes et plus complètes, ce qui nous permet d'être plus confiants dans la conclusion selon laquelle l'exposition aux ondes radio des technologies sans fil ne constitue pas un danger pour la santé humaine.
Ni la durée d'exposition, ni l'intensité d'usage, y compris sur des périodes supérieures à dix ans, ne modifient le constat. Les données sur le cancer cérébral ont reçu le niveau de certitude le plus élevé possible pour des études observationnelles. Autre peur récurrente mise en pièces : la proximité d'antennes de radio ou de télévision et la leucémie infantile. Là encore, aucun signal statistiquement significatif.
Des zones d'ombre persistent, mais le tableau d'ensemble rassure
L'OMS n'a pas encore achevé sa propre analyse globale de ces 13 revues, et Diepstraten et La Marca reconnaissent que, pour de nombreux effets sanitaires (fertilité, acouphènes, céphalées), la qualité ou le volume des preuves reste insuffisant pour trancher. Le travail des chercheurs du WEHI offre cependant un aperçu solide des conclusions attendues.
Même si l'usage du téléphone portable a explosé au cours des 20 dernières années, il n'y a pas eu d'augmentation correspondante des cancers du cerveau ni d'aucun autre cancer de la tête ou du cou.
L'argument épidémiologique de fond est d'ailleurs implacable : si les ondes du mobile causaient réellement des tumeurs cérébrales, on observerait une flambée d'incidence après deux décennies d'adoption planétaire. Or c'est exactement l'inverse qui se produit : les taux de cancers du cerveau ont diminué. De quoi conforter les limites d'exposition actuelles, en attendant que l'OMS referme officiellement le dossier.

articles.title: "No es trampa, es ingeniería": así elude China 2.000 patentes de ASML con un truco láser
articles.text:
La litografía de ultravioleta extremo (UVE) es el cuello de botella más estrecho de toda la industria de los semiconductores. Solo una compañía en el mundo, la neerlandesa ASML, fabrica estas máquinas, imprescindibles para producir circuitos integrados por debajo de los 7 nm, y desde 2019 tiene prohibido vender sus modelos más avanzados a China por presión de EEUU. Cada equipo cuesta entre 200 y 400 millones de dólares, y hasta ahora ni un solo cliente chino ha logrado hacerse con uno.
Un equipo de la Academia China de Ciencias, con sede en el Instituto de Óptica y Mecánica de Precisión de Shanghái, ha construido la primera plataforma china de fuente de luz UVE por láser-plasma. Al frente está Lin Nan, excientífico de ASML y responsable técnico de sus fuentes de luz para metrología, que regresó a China en 2021 dentro de un programa estatal de atracción de talento. Su equipo ha optado por una vía que esquiva deliberadamente el método de ASML, así como más de 2.000 de sus patentes.
Qiu Yanfang, columnista china especializada en semiconductores, lo ha resumido sin ambigüedad: este rodeo de patentes no es solo una maniobra legal; es ingeniería genuina. Y es esta valoración, publicada hace apenas dos semanas, la que ha vuelto a poner el foco sobre hasta dónde ha llegado realmente China en su carrera por la independencia tecnológica en litografía.
El camino más largo hasta la producción en masa
El truco técnico consiste en lo siguiente: mientras ASML genera luz UVE disparando potentes láseres de dióxido de carbono contra gotas de estaño en movimiento (un método conocido como LPP), el equipo de Lin Nan utiliza un láser de estado sólido de 1 micra que golpea un blanco de estaño sólido. En un artículo publicado en diciembre de 2024, Lin y su equipo ya defendían que este tipo de láseres podía sustituir a los de dióxido de carbono como fuente de próxima generación gracias a su tamaño compacto y su mayor eficiencia de conversión.
No obstante, la propia Qiu Yanfang matiza su entusiasmo inicial. A corto plazo, sostiene, esta fuente de estado sólido no puede sacudir el dominio de ASML, ya que toda la industria global de los semiconductores ha construido sus cadenas de suministro, sus patentes y su experiencia de ingeniería alrededor del láser de dióxido de carbono. Aunque la tecnología china logre resultados en el laboratorio, todavía le queda un largo trecho hasta alcanzar la producción a gran escala. El valor real del logro de Lin, en cualquier caso, reside en sentar las bases y forjar un equipo de investigación que cubra desde la teoría hasta la ingeniería aplicada.
El Gobierno chino aspira a producir chips con esta tecnología en 2028, aunque buena parte de los analistas considera 2030 una fecha más realista
Este esfuerzo convive, además, con otra vía paralela y mucho más hermética. Según reveló Reuters en diciembre de 2025, China ha montado un prototipo de máquina UVE operativo dentro de un laboratorio de alta seguridad en Shenzhen, aunque todavía no fabrica circuitos integrados funcionales.
Huawei coordina esta iniciativa, que involucra a miles de ingenieros: el Instituto de Tecnología de Harbin se encarga de la fuente de luz, el Instituto de Óptica de Changchún de los sistemas ópticos, y SMEE (Shanghai Micro Electronics Equipment) de la integración final, con SiCarrier (la empresa china respaldada por el Gobierno de Shenzhen y vinculada a Huawei) como otro de los actores clave. El Gobierno chino aspira a producir chips con esta tecnología en 2028, aunque buena parte de los analistas considera 2030 una fecha más realista.
Por ahora ningún prototipo chino ha demostrado ser capaz de fabricar circuitos integrados comerciales con litografía UVE propia, y las dudas sobre la velocidad real de este avance han vuelto a la primera línea informativa por otro motivo muy distinto. El secretario de Comercio de EEUU, Howard Lutnick, ha planteado a directivos sénior de ASML la posibilidad de que uno de sus equipos UVE haya llegado a China por canales clandestinos, algo que la compañía neerlandesa ha negado de forma rotunda: ninguna de sus 314 máquinas UVE operativas en el mundo, ni ninguna de las 26 ya retiradas, se encuentra en territorio chino.
China no tiene todavía su máquina UVE. Pero, gracias a Lin Nan, ya tiene algo que hasta hace poco tampoco tenía: un camino propio para intentar construirla.

articles.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra et Z Flip 8 : où les précommander au meilleur prix
articles.text:
Les nouveaux pliables de Samsung sont enfin dévoilés, et la course aux meilleures offres de précommande a déjà commencé. Entre bonus exclusifs et remises sur le stockage, voici où précommander le Galaxy Z Fold 8, le Z Fold 8 Ultra et le Z Flip 8 au meilleur prix.
Ce mercredi 22 juillet 2026, Samsung a présenté sa nouvelle génération de smartphones pliants lors de l'événement Galaxy Unpacked. Le constructeur coréen a cette fois dévoilé trois modèles : le Galaxy Z Fold 8, le tout nouveau Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra positionné en haut de gamme absolu, et le Galaxy Z Flip 8 dans son format clapet désormais familier. Les précommandes sont ouvertes dès l'annonce, avec plusieurs bonus exclusifs à la clé selon le marchand choisi.
Pourquoi précommander les nouveaux smartphones pliants Samsung ?
Précommander l'un de ces trois smartphones permet de cumuler plusieurs avantages exclusifs proposés par Samsung, valables pour chacun des trois modèles. Ces bonus s'ajoutent aux éventuelles remises pratiquées par les différents marchands, rendant la précommande particulièrement avantageuse par rapport à un achat après le lancement officiel.
- 6 mois d'abonnement à Google AI Pro offerts pour l'achat de n'importe lequel des trois modèles
- Une Mystery Box offerte, contenant des produits divers pour une valeur totale pouvant atteindre 568 euros
- 100 euros de remise sur les versions 512 Go, et 200 euros de remise sur les versions 1 To, sur le site officiel Samsung
| Modèle | Stockage | Prix officiel de lancement | Prix avec bonus stockage Samsung Store | 
| Galaxy Z Flip 8 | 256 Go | 1 299 € | — | 
| Galaxy Z Flip 8 | 512 Go | 1 499 € | — | 
| Galaxy Z Fold 8 | 256 Go | 1 999 € | — | 
| Galaxy Z Fold 8 | 512 Go | 2 199 € | 1 999 € (- 200 €) | 
| Galaxy Z Fold 8 | 1 To | 2 399 € | 2 199 € (- 200 €) | 
| Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra | 256 Go | 2 199 € | — | 
| Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra | 512 Go | 2 399 € | 2 199 € (- 200 €) | 
| Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra | 1 To | 2 799 € | 2 399 € (- 400 €) | 
Le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 est le moins cher des deux modèles grand écran, avec un tarif de lancement fixé à 1 999 € en version 256 Go, contre 2 199 € pour le Z Fold 8 Ultra à capacité équivalente. Ce dernier assume clairement son statut de modèle le plus complet et le plus premium de toute la gamme, avec un tarif pouvant grimper jusqu'à 2 799 € en version 1 To.
Mais c'est bien le Galaxy Z Flip 8 qui reste, toutes catégories confondues, le smartphone pliant le plus abordable de la nouvelle gamme Samsung, avec un prix de lancement débutant à 1 299 €, bien en dessous des deux Z Fold, même s'il subit lui aussi une hausse notable de 100 à 180 € par rapport à la génération précédente.
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8
Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 reprend le format pliant grand écran qui a fait le succès de la gamme, avec un tarif de lancement fixé à 1 999 euros pour la version 256 Go. La version 512 Go est proposée à 2 199 euros et la version 1 To à 2 399 euros, avant application des remises de précommande sur le stockage. Grâce au bonus Samsung, la version 512 Go revient donc à 2 099 euros et la version 1 To à 2 199 euros directement sur le site officiel de la marque.
Ce modèle reste le point d'entrée le plus accessible de la nouvelle gamme pliante, tout en conservant les fonctionnalités phares de la série Z Fold. Il est disponible en précommande sur plusieurs canaux :
- Samsung Store : précommande officielle avec cumul de tous les bonus (Google AI Pro, Mystery Box, remise stockage)
- Amazon : disponible en précommande avec une remise directe de 200 €
- Boulanger : précommande avec remise immédiate de 200 euros pour les membres du Club INFINITY, ainsi qu'un bonus reprise de 200 euros
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra
Nouveauté de cette édition, le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra vient compléter la gamme en se positionnant comme le modèle le plus haut de gamme jamais proposé par Samsung dans la catégorie des pliables grand format. Son tarif de lancement démarre à 2 199 euros pour la version 256 Go, 2 399 euros pour la version 512 Go et 2 799 euros pour la version 1 To. Avec les remises de précommande sur le site Samsung, la version 512 Go revient à 2 299 euros et la version 1 To à 2 599 euros.
Ce modèle Ultra cible les utilisateurs les plus exigeants, prêts à investir davantage pour bénéficier des dernières technologies embarquées par Samsung sur cette génération. Il est disponible en précommande sur les mêmes canaux que le modèle standard :
- Samsung Store : précommande officielle avec cumul intégral des bonus, dont la remise stockage particulièrement intéressante sur ce modèle premium
- Amazon : disponible en précommande avec une remise directe de 200 €
- Boulanger : mêmes avantages Club INFINITY que sur le Z Fold 8, avec remise immédiate de 200 euros et bonus reprise associé
Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8
Le Galaxy Z Flip 8 poursuit l'évolution du format clapet compact, qui continue de séduire les utilisateurs en quête d'un smartphone premium plus discret et facile à glisser dans une poche. Comme pour les deux autres modèles, les bonus de précommande Samsung s'appliquent intégralement, avec la remise stockage qui rend d'autant plus intéressant le passage à une version supérieure de mémoire.
Ce modèle reste l'option la plus accessible de la nouvelle gamme pliante 2026, tout en conservant l'ADN clapet qui a fait le succès de la lignée Z Flip. Il est disponible en précommande sur :
- Samsung Store : précommande officielle avec l'ensemble des bonus cumulables (Google AI Pro, Mystery Box, remise stockage)
- Amazon : disponible en précommande avec une remise directe de 200 €
- Boulanger : avantages Club INFINITY applicables, avec remise et bonus reprise sur ce modèle également

articles.title: Gen Z vertraut KI-Chatbots in Finanzfragen – vielleicht zu sehr?
articles.text:
Gen Z vertraut bei Finanzfragen auf KI-Chatbots: Warum das ein Problem ist
OpenAI ermöglicht es Nutzer:innen seines KI-Chatbots ChatGPT seit Mai 2026, ihre Bankkonten zu verknüpfen und sich finanziellen Rat zu Ausgaben und Sparmöglichkeiten einzuholen. Besonders junge Leute sehen in der Technologie eine Alternative für ihre persönlichen Finanzangelegenheiten.
Gen Z bei KI-Nutzung in Finanzfragen vorn
Einer von Techradar zitierten aktuellen Umfrage des britischen Marktforschungsinstituts Opinium zufolge nutzen schon 80 Prozent der Gen-Z-Angehörigen, die sich mit Finanzfragen beschäftigen, KI für entsprechende Ratschläge. Die Zahlen sind in Deutschland ähnlich, wie eine Bitkom-Umfrage im Mai 2026 ergeben hat. Demnach liegt die Gen Z bei der KI-Nutzung für finanzielle Angelegenheiten weit vor anderen Altersgruppen wie Baby-Boomern oder Gen X.
Wie die Opinium-Ergebnisse ebenfalls zeigen, geht es dabei nicht nur um die Klärung von Fragen im Finanzbereich. 58 Prozent der Befragten lassen sich von KI-Chatbots wie ChatGPT oder Gemini auch konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen für zukünftige Investitionen geben.
Dazu kommt, dass nur 29 Prozent der investitionsfreudigen Gen-Z-Angehörigen den KI-generierten Informationen nicht trauen. Zum Vergleich: Über alle Altersklassen hinweg sind es 49 Prozent.
Anlagetipps von Chatbots: Gratis und bequem
Die Gründe dafür, dass sich vor allem junge Menschen Anlagetipps von KI-Chatbots geben lassen, sind so einfach wie nachvollziehbar. 43 Prozent der Befragten gaben an, dass sie in Finanzfragen KI-Tools nutzen, weil der Einstieg kostenlos sei. 41 Prozent wiederum schätzten, dass die KI-Anlageberatung schnell und bequem sei.
Auf der anderen Seite senken KI-Chatbots auch die Hürden für den Einstieg in die Beschäftigung mit Anlagemöglichkeiten. So gaben 38 Prozent der weiblichen und 27 Prozent der männlichen Nutzer:innen an, dass sie sich wohler damit fühlten, einen Chatbot als eine echte Person um Ratschläge zu bitten. Laut Opinium könnten Chatbots gerade bei Anfänger:innen die Scham verringern, die diese beim Stellen einfacher Fragen empfinden könnten.
Junge investieren früher und häufiger
Grundsätzlich sind die jungen Menschen der Gen Z aber ohnehin deutlich aktiver, was das Investieren und die finanzielle Vorsorge angeht. Das hat eine Mitte Juli 2026 veröffentlichte Barclays-Studie herausgefunden. Demnach zahlen junge Brit:innen im Schnitt zwölfmal pro Jahr Geld auf ihre Depots ein – deutlich öfter als Millennials, Gen X oder Baby-Boomer. Die höhere Affinität zu dem Thema lässt sich demnach auch damit begründen, dass in den vergangenen Jahren der Zugang über Apps und Plattformen einfacher geworden ist.
Aber: Die Angehörigen der Gen Z fühlen sich laut Studie auch unsicher, was Themen wie Risiko, Diversifikation oder langfristige Anlagestrategien angeht. Es könnte also durchaus sein, dass die jungen Menschen diese Wissenslücken per KI-Chatbot schließen wollen.
Kann KI besser erklären als ein Mensch?
In der eingangs erwähnten Bitkom-Umfrage zeigten sich 30 Prozent der Befragten davon überzeugt, dass KI Finanzthemen besser erklären kann als ein Mensch. Knapp ein Viertel vertraut KI mehr als einer menschlichen Finanzberatung. Das birgt Risiken. Können doch KI-Chatbots durch Halluzinationen oder unter Zuhilfenahme unseriöser Quellen schnell falsche Informationen liefern.
Daher pochen Expert:innen wie Bitkom-Präsident Ralf Wintergerst darauf, dass „KI-Anwendungen gerade hier transparent, sicher und in ihren Aussagen nachvollziehbar“ sein sollten. Nutzer:innen sollten gerade bei größeren Summen vorgeschlagene Anlagestrategien vergleichen und die KI-Angaben mit seriösen Quellen abgleichen.

articles.title: Nvidia reveals Vera CPU details, claims its custom Olympus cores outperform AMD Epyc Turin
articles.text:
What just happened? Nvidia has released more information about its upcoming Vera data center CPU this week, including key details about the custom Olympus cores that are purpose-built for agentic AI workloads. The company also claimed that the new core architecture offers faster single-core performance than competing products.
Part of Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, the Arm-based Vera CPU is designed to perform complex reasoning, facilitate tool execution, generate code, and plan tasks for AI agents. Developed as a multi-purpose chip, it can also handle scientific data processing and reinforcement learning, which demand more CPU power than typical AI workloads.
Each Vera CPU incorporates 88 Olympus cores, 176 physical threads, a 64KB four-way L1 instruction cache, and 164MB of unified L3 cache on a monolithic compute die. It also features a 48-instruction decode queue. The mid-core incorporates a 96KB six-way L1 data cache and a 2MB eight-way L2 cache, alongside a hardware graph prefetcher for data-intensive graph and analytics workloads.
Each custom core comprise a wide front-end with optimized branch predictors, a mid-core with critical path acceleration, and an execution engine with complex vector optimization. They offer high-bandwidth instruction fetch supporting up to 16 instructions per cycle and include a 10-wide decode engine processing up to ten fused instructions per cycle.
Olympus' branch prediction subsystem includes a neural branch predictor capable of reducing wrong-path execution on specific branch patterns. Combined with the wide decode path, it also helps improve front-end throughput for latency-sensitive workloads, such as agentic AI and reinforcement learning.
The Olympus core architecture integrates Nvidia's Spatial Multithreading technology, enabling flexible resource partitioning. It also supports the Scalable Coherency Fabric for 3.4 TB/s of on-die core-to-core bandwidth, 1.2 TB/s of aggregate SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X memory bandwidth, and up to 1.5 TB of memory capacity.
Vera supports 1.8 TB/s connectivity on NVLink-C2C, PCIe 6.4, and CXL 3.1. It supports dual-socket scaling, too, with each socket providing 176 PCIe Gen 6 lanes. To improve latency in dual-socket systems, Vera uses a software-based solution where each socket presents itself as a single NUMA domain, avoiding fragmentation and creating a clean two-NUMA-node topology.
To back up its claims about Vera's performance, Nvidia published its internal SPEC CPU 2026 test results from earlier this month. The data seems to show that Vera delivers up to 1.8 times the performance of AMD's Epyc Turin 9755 systems in select agentic AI workloads, such as 714.cpython_r. However, the results have yet to be independently verified.

articles.title: Senior White House official accuses Moonshot AI of copying Anthropic's leading frontier model - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Senior White House official accuses Moonshot AI of copying Anthropic’s leading frontier model
A senior White House official has accused Chinese artificial intelligence startup Moonshot AI of using so-called “distillation” techniques to essentially pirate the capabilities of Anthropic PBC’s most powerful models in its own, open-source AI systems.
“We have information that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic’s Fable for the development of its K3 model,” Michael Kratsios (pictured), director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said in a post on X on Wednesday.
Kratsios was referring to Moonshot AI’s new Kimi K3 model, which was pronounced the world’s largest open-weights model when it was released last week to great fanfare thanks to its prowess, which matches some of the capabilities of Anthropic’s and OpenAI Group PBC’s best AI systems. He added that the company went to great lengths to hide what it had done.
“To do this they developed a sophisticated internal platform to conduct large-scale distillation against U.S. models, allowing them to quickly switch between multiple methods of access to avoid detection,” he claimed.
Experts say Kimi K3 is the most advanced open-weights model released so far, performing at the same level, or sometimes even above that of other leading frontier models in multiple benchmarks. But whereas Anthropic and OpenAI intend to charge for access to their best models, having spent billions of dollars to develop them, Moonshot AI plans to make Kimi K3 freely available for anyone to download, run and customize on their own servers or devices.
What did Moonshot AI allegedly do?
Kratsios claims that Moonshot AI used a machine learning compression method known as distillation to transfer knowledge from Fable 5 to Kimi K3. In distillation, a larger “teacher” model is used to train a smaller “student” model. Rather than learn only from basic right-or-wrong answers, the student model learns from the teacher model’s full probability distributions – for instance, a 90% chance for word A, 8% for word B – which reveal clues about how the teacher thinks.
Distillation is sometimes used in “legitimate” ways, Kratsios said. For instance, some AI labs use the technique to train less powerful models on the outputs of a more powerful one to make more efficient versions of the same AI systems. “Legitimate AI distillation used to create smaller, more efficient models plays a vital role in this open innovation ecosystem,” he said. “However, large-scale, covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing proprietary U.S. technology and undermining American research is unacceptable.”
Kratsios’ comments come just days after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the U.S. government could sanction Chinese AI model makers if proof emerges that they basically copied American-made models to develop their own. They’re notable, because they represent a rare instance in which the Trump administration has appeared to be supportive of Anthropic.
There has been a lot of antagonism between the White House and the AI firm recently, with officials recently preventing the company from releasing Fable 5 due to security concerns. Prior to that, in February, the Pentagon blacklisted Anthropic after it was refused full access to its leading frontier models.
“Thanks @mkratsios47 for speaking out on this important issue,” Sarah Heck, Anthropic’s head of public policy, wrote in a reply to Kratsios’s post on X.
Heck added that Anthropic is continuing to work with the government to try to prevent U.S. models from being distilled by Chinese firms. “Illicit, adversarial distillation is IP theft and industrial espionage that supports adversary military and intelligence capabilities,” she wrote. “It is a national challenge that creates serious national security risks for the United States and democratic allies.”
Anthropic first accused Chinese firms of abusing the distillation process in February, pointing fingers at Moonshot AI, MiniMax and DeepSeek Ltd. and calling on the U.S. government to take action to prevent it. But while White House officials paid lip service, Anthropic did not get much sympathy from the general public, which noted the irony of the allegations, given that it trained its systems on massive volumes of copyrighted data posted online.
Experts are skeptical
Despite getting Kratsios’ support, there are many who believe that distillation cannot be responsible for the advanced capabilities of Kimi K3. For instance, Braden Hancock, a researcher at the Laude Institute and the co-founder of AI startup Snorkel AI Inc., told TechCrunch that it would be almost impossible to train a model as strong as Kimi K3 on Fable 5 so quickly. “There’s just not even frankly time, right?” he said. “Fable’s only been publicly available since July 1st. You can’t distill that much data, train a model, and release it in two weeks.”
Another expert, Nathan Lambert, who is a researcher at the Allen Institute for AI, was similarly skeptical that Moonshot AI could have pulled it off so quickly. “I’ve been of the opinion that distillation has becoming less and less impactful over time as the Chinese models get closer to the frontier and the training regime shifts to [reinforcement learning],” he said in a podcast this week. “[If] it were the case, everyone would be easily able to catch up to a GLM or to a K3 by using its data for distillation. But we have not, or we won’t see this, from supervised fine-tuning alone.”
Given that the White House claims to have “evidence” of Moonshot AI’s guilt, the next question is whether the government will actually follow through on Bessent’s threat to start sanctioning Chinese AI companies. Moonshot AI has not commented on the allegations, but a spokesperson at the Chinese embassy in Washington D.C. told Reuters that the claims are “entirely unfounded.”
“Relevant individuals in the United States should respect the facts, discard prejudice and stop smearing and discrediting China’s achievements in the development of its artificial intelligence industry,” the spokesperson said.

articles.title: Como criar um convite virtual interativo: 6 opções com lista de convidados • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como criar um convite virtual interativo: 6 opções com lista de convidados
Convite virtual interativo é uma página que centraliza as informações de um evento, permitindo gerenciar a lista de convidados e automatizar a confirmação de presença
Os serviços de convite virtual interativo facilitam organizar qualquer evento, reunindo dados e atualizações em uma página fácil de compartilhar. O recurso permite centralizar tudo, desde a confirmação de presença até os detalhes do encontro, em um único link acessível.
Essa tecnologia simplifica o planejamento, automatizando a gestão por meio do sistema de RSVP, permitindo que cada convidado confirme a presença com poucos cliques. Assim, o organizador garante controle exato do público para um convite de aniversário ou reunião corporativa sem estresse.
A seguir, conheça 6 serviços de convite virtual interativo para planejar seus eventos e comemorações.
Voltado para eventos profissionais, venda de ingressos, controle de capacidade.
Partiful
O Partiful é uma plataforma de gestão de eventos (event hub) disponível na web e mobile que substitui convites tradicionais e grupos de conversa por páginas visuais e interativas.
Como funciona: o anfitrião cria a página personalizada do evento e gera um link de compartilhamento. Os convidados confirmam presença via RSVP em poucos cliques direto no navegador, sem precisar baixar o app ou criar conta.
Principais funções: gestão de convidados, questionários para restrições alimentares, envio de convite via SMS, murais interativos para compartilhamento de fotos e mensagens, integração com plataformas de vaquinhas e arrecadação.
Indicado para: festas de aniversários, encontros em casa, jantares, clubes de leitura, happy hours e celebrações de pequeno a médio porte.
É gratuito?: sim, todas as ferramentas de criação, confirmação de presença e mensagens são gratuitas para anfitriões e convidados.
Convites Apple
O Convites Apple é uma plataforma integrada ao ecossistema iOS e à web para centralizar o planejamento de eventos sociais por meio de páginas interativas.
Como funciona: o organizador cria o convite no aplicativo ou pelo navegador via iCloud e compartilha o link via iMessage ou WhatsApp. Os convidados acessam via web e confirmam presença sem precisar de Conta Apple ou do app.
Principais funções: gestão de lista de convidados em tempo real, páginas personalizadas com fotos e trilha sonora via Apple Music, álbum de fotos colaborativo, informações de rotas via Apple Maps e previsão de tempo para o dia do evento.
Indicado para: encontros informais, aniversários, jantares em família, churrascos e até casamentos.
É gratuito?: a criação de eventos exige uma assinatura paga do iCloud+, mas o uso é gratuito para os convidados visualizarem e confirmarem presença.
FestaLab
O FestaLab é uma plataforma web de event hub brasileira especializada na criação de páginas de eventos para centralizar convites, confirmações de presença e lista de presentes.
Como funciona: o anfitrião personaliza um modelo no navegador e compartilha o link do convite digital por WhatsApp ou redes sociais. Os convidados acessam a página interativa sem precisar baixar aplicativos.
Principais funções: painel de controle de confirmações (RSVP) em tempo real, mural de recados e mensagens no evento, lista de presentes integrada com a plataforma Vinklo e envio de convites com design otimizado para dispositivos móveis.
Indicado para: casamentos, chás de bebê, chás revelação, aniversários infantis e formaturas.
É gratuito?: a criação da página de evento e controle de presença são gratuitos, sendo cobrada apenas uma taxa percentual nas doações e presentes convertidos em dinheiro.
Convitin
O Convite é um serviço web brasileiro para criação de páginas de eventos que reúne convite virtual, confirmação de presença e a lista de presentes em um único link.
Como funciona: o organizador edita um modelo personalizável pelo navegador e compartilha o link do convite por mensagem. O convidado acessa a página e confirma presença sem precisar instalar apps.
Principais funções: painel de controle de confirmações com nomes pré-cadastrados, regras para limite de acompanhantes, lista virtual de presentes integrada para arrecadação financeira, mural de mensagens e recados dos convidados.
Indicado para: casamentos, festas de aniversários, chás de bebê, datas comemorativas e eventos corporativos de pequeno porte.
É gratuito?: a criação da página de convite interativo, o controle de convidados e arrecadação de presentes são gratuitos, com repasses via Pix sem cobranças de taxas.
Evite
O Evite é uma plataforma web e aplicativo para criação, envio e gerenciamento de convites digitais e cartões comemorativos para eventos pessoais e corporativos.
Como funciona: o anfitrião edita um modelo pelo painel do hub e envia o link de convite por e-mail, SMS ou redes sociais. Os convidados respondem na página e os dados atualizam em tempo real.
Principais funções: milhares de modelos customizáveis, gestão avançada com rastreamento de presença (RSVP), limite de acompanhantes por convite, check-in por QR Code no local e feed interativo para compartilhamento de fotos pós-evento.
É gratuito?: oferece plano gratuito com envio ilimitado de convites com exibição de anúncios, e uma versão Premium paga por evento para remover propagandas e liberar modelos exclusivos.
Luma
Luma é uma plataforma web e mobile voltada para o design de páginas de eventos, gestão de convidados e venda de ingressos.
Como funciona: o anfitrião cria a página do evento e envia convites em massa por e-mail ou SMS. Os participantes confirmam presença e recebem um passe digital com QR Code para acesso.
Principais funções: painel de controle de participantes com aprovação manual, envio de lembretes, check-in por QR Code, sistema de venda de ingressos, coleta de doações, integração com Zoom e Google Agenda para links automáticos de reuniões.
Indicado para: encontros profissionais e sociais, workshops, webinars, lançamentos de produtos, aulas e eventos sociais de comunidades.
É gratuito: a criação de convites e gestão de eventos são gratuitos, cobrando apenas uma taxa percentual sobre a venda de ingressos pagos.
O que significa RSVP no convite virtual?
RSVP é a sigla da expressão francesa “Répondez s’il vous plaît” (“Responda, por favor”, em português). Esse conceito foi adaptado ao ecossistema digital como um botão interativo para a confirmação de presença do convidado.
Quando a pessoa escolhe uma das opções (Sim, Não ou Talvez), os dados são atualizados na plataforma de controle do anfitrião. Além da confirmação, essas informações são essenciais para, por exemplo, ajustar o cálculo exato de buffet, bebidas e a logística do local.
Qual a vantagem de criar um convite virtual interativo?
Estas são as principais vantagens de apostar em um convite virtual interativo:
Atualização em tempo real: permite embutir mapas interativos e cronogramas em um único link, garantindo que qualquer alteração de local ou horário seja sincronizada instantaneamente e sem precisar reenviar novos convites;
Gestão de RSVP automatizada: centraliza o controle de confirmações em um painel (dashboard), coletando dados essenciais como número de acompanhantes e restrições alimentares;
Engajamento e expectativa: aumenta a interatividade do público antes do evento por meio de recursos como contagem regressiva, galerias de fotos, playlists e murais de recados;
Disparos e lembretes instantâneos: facilita o envio em massa por e-mail ou aplicativos de mensagem, permitindo monitorar a taxa de abertura e programar notificações automáticas;
Relatórios simplificados: permite exportar a lista final de convidados em arquivos organizados, simplificando a integração com sistemas de credenciamento e check-in.
O que acontece se eu apagar o convite virtual?
O impacto de apagar um convite virtual depende de quem executa a ação. Em geral, quando o anfitrião deleta o evento, a página é excluída, tornando o link inativo e apagando dados do painel, como relatórios e arquivos de mídia.
Já para o convidado, apagar a mensagem ou e-mail apenas limpa a caixa de entrada, sem alterar o status no sistema de controle do anfitrião. Por isso, a recusa do RSVP deve ser feita diretamente na plataforma para atualizar a lista.

Construiu experiência na área ao produzir notícias diárias sobre eletrônicos (celulares, vestíveis), inovação, mercado e conteúdos especiais sobre os temas. É repórter do Tecnoblog desde outubro de 2023. Anteriormente, atuou como redator de tecnologia e entretenimento no TecMundo (2019-2021/2022-2023) e redator de produtos no Canaltech (2021-2022).

Lucas Lima trabalha no Tecnoblog desde 2019 cobrindo software, hardware e serviços. Formou-se em Jornalismo em 2018 e concluiu o técnico em Informática em 2014, mas respira tecnologia desde 2006, quando ganhou o primeiro computador e varava noites abrindo janelas do Windows XP. articles.title: Microsoft announces Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC — will let gamers play classic console games on PCs and handhelds
articles.text:
Microsoft announces Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC — will let gamers play classic console games on PCs and handhelds
Including the new Xbox ROG Ally lineup
Xbox has announced a new Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC program, which will let gamers play a selection of classic Xbox titles on PCs and handhelds, a move the company says marks the beginning of a bigger push into Xbox game preservation. The announcement begins with four titles that can now be played on PCs and handhelds, including the ROG Xbox Ally and Ally X.
"This marks the beginning of a broader effort to preserve XBOX games from the past and bring them to PC over time," the company said in a blog post authored by Xbox "VP next generation" Jason Ronald. Alongside backward compatibility, the company says games will also include new features. The four titles in the announcement are:
You can now buy all of these games on PC, and they're also included in all Xbox Game Pass plans. Anyone who already owns these titles digitally on console can also now play them on PC or handheld, with support for Xbox Play Anywhere and Xbox Cloud Gaming. Crucially, this appears to be a digital-only preservation effort, so it won't help anyone who only owns physical copies of these games. Xbox has reportedly been testing a way to digitize physical games as far back as Xbox One, but that hasn't yet materialized yet.
Alongside the preserved original gameplay, Xbox claims these games will let users customize graphics settings, with up to 4x resolution scaling, VSync support, Fullscreen and Windowed modes, anisotropic filtering, and enhanced anti-aliasing, with more features to come in the future. Notably, Xbox will add achievements to select original Xbox games on console and PC.
Users who want to play these titles will need to meet the following system requirements:
| Spec: | Minimum requirements | Recommended specs | 
| GPU | Nvidia GTX 950 or AMD Radeon RX 550 or Intel UHD 770 or Intel Arc A310 | Radeon RX 68005 or Nvidia GTX 1070 Ti or Intel Arc A770 | 
| CPU | Min 4 Cores Intel Core i3-8100 or AMD Ryzen 3 1200 or AMD Ryzen Z2 A Processor | 6 cores and 12 threads Intel Core i5-10400 or AMD Ryzen 5 3600 or AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme | 
| RAM | 8GB | 8GB | 
| DirectX | N/A | DirectX12 API, Hardware Feature Level 11 | 
| OS | Windows 11 | Windows 11 | 
| Drivers | Latest Version as of January 2026 | Latest Version as of January 2026 | 
Microsoft's emphasis on preserving older games is particularly noteworthy given recent backlash against Sony over its decision to end physical games with its next console generation, and the shuttering of some of its online stores. While Xbox's digital emphasis on game preservation still can't match the solidarity of physical media preservation, the timing of this announcement seems like more than just a coincidence.
